name: Boat
description: From a seated position the feet are lifted up so that the thighs are angled about 45-50 degrees relative to the earth. The tailbone is lengthened into the earth and the pubis pulls toward the navel. The shoulder blades are spread across the back and the hands reach around the back of the calves, with legs pulled towards the body. The chin is tipped slightly toward the sternum so that the base of the skull lifts lightly away from the back of the neck. Gaze is forward.
benefits: Strengthens the abdomen, hip flexors, and spine. Stimulates the kidneys, thyroid and prostate glands, and intestines. Helps relieve stress. Improves digestion.

name: Half Boat
translation: ardha = half, nāva = boat, āsana = posture
description: From a seated position the hands are gripped around the back of the legs and the knees are bent in a 90 degree angle. Both legs are pulled in towards the abdomen. The core is engaged to maintain balance on the sits bones (be sure that the back does not round). The front of the torso lengthens between the pubis and top of the sternum as the spine extends in both directions reaching up to the sky and rooting down to the earth. The gaze is forward and Bandhas are engaged.
benefits: Strengthens the abdomen, hip flexors and spine. Stimulates the kidneys, thyroid, prostate glands and intestines. Helps relieve stress. Improves digestion.

name: Bow
description: From a prone position with the abdomen on the earth, the hands grip the ankles (but not the tops of the feet) with knees no wider than the width of your hips. The heels are lifted away from the buttocks and at the same time the thighs are lifted away from the earth working opposing forces as the heart center, hips and back open. The gaze is forward.
benefits: Stretches the entire front of the body, ankles, thighs and groins, abdomen and chest, and throat, and deep hip flexors (psoas). Strengthens the back muscles. Improves posture. Stimulates the organs of the abdomen and neck.

name: Bridge
translation: setu = bridge, bandha = lock, sarva = all, āṅga = limb, āsana = posture
description: From a supine position, on your back, the hips are pressed up with the heels of the feet rooted into the earth close to the sits bones. The toes are actively lifted and the pelvis tucked. The thighs are parallel to the earth and the fingers are interlaced under the body with the ribcage lifted and the heart open. The back of the neck rests on the earth. The gaze is to the sky.
benefits: Stretches the chest, neck, and spine. Stimulates abdominal organs, lungs, and thyroids. Rejuvenates tired legs. Improves digestion. Helps relieve the symptoms of menopause. Relieves menstrual discomfort when done supported. Reduces anxiety, fatigue, backache, headache, and insomnia. Therapeutic for asthma, high blood pressure, osteoporosis, and sinusitis.

name: Butterfly
translation: baddha = bound, koṇa = angle, āsana = posture
description: In sitting position, bend both knees and drop the knees to each side, opening the hips. Bring the soles of the feet together and bring the heels as close to the groin as possible, keeping the knees close to the ground. The hands may reach down and grasp and maneuver the feet so that the soles are facing upwards and the heels and little toes are connected. The shoulders should be pulled back and no rounding of the spine.
benefits: Opens the hips and groins. Stretches the shoulders, rib cage and back. Stimulates the abdominal organs, lungs and heart.

name: Camel
description: From a kneeling position the knees are hip width apart and the thighs are perpendicular to the earth. The inner thighs are narrowed and rotated slightly inward with the buttocks engaged but not hardened. The tailbone is tucked under but the hips do not puff forward. The shins and tops of the feet are pressed firmly into the earth. The ribcage is open, along with the heart center, but the lower front ribs do not protrude sharply towards the sky. The lower back lifts the ribs away from the pelvis to keep the lower spine as long as possible. The base of the palms are pressed firmly against the soles (or heels) of the feet and the fingers are pointed toward the toes. The arms are extended straight and are turned slightly outward at the shoulder joint so the elbow creases face forward without squeezing the shoulder blades together. The neck is in a relatively neutral position, neither flexed nor extended, or (for the advanced practitioners only) the head drops back. Be careful not to strain your neck and harden your throat. The gaze is either towards the sky or towards the earth, depending upon your flexibility.
benefits: Stretches the entire front of the body, the ankles, thighs and groins, abdomen and chest, and throat. Stretches the deep hip flexors (psoas). Strengthens back muscles. Improves posture. Stimulates the organs of the abdomen and neck.

name: Cat
description: From box neutral shift some weight to the palms. The wrists, elbows and shoulders are in one line. The abdomen is pulled in and up with the spine arched in a strong Cobra spine. The crown of the head is towards the earth and the neck is relaxed. The gaze is between the arms towards the belly.
benefits: Relieves the spine and neck. Energizes the body.

name: Cow
description: From box neutral the ribcage is lifted with a gentle sway in the low back. The tailbone lifts up into dog tilt. The eyes are soft and the gaze is to the sky.
benefits: Removes fatigue. Improves breathing and the circulation of blood to the brain. Rejuvenates the entire body.

name: Chair
description: From a standing position, the feet are together and rooted into the earth with toes actively lifted. The knees are bent and the weight of the body is on the heels of the feet. The pelvis is tucked in and the ribcage is lifted. The neck is a natural extension of the spine. The arms are lifted up toward the sky with the elbows straight and the biceps by the ears. The hands can be together or separated and facing each other with the fingers spread wide. The gaze is forward.
benefits: Strengthens the ankles, thighs, calves, and spine. Stretches shoulders and chest. Stimulates the abdominal organs, diaphragm, and heart. Reduces flat feet. Energizes the entire body.

name: Child's Pose
description: From a kneeling position, the toes and knees are together with most of the weight of the body resting on the heels of the feet. The arms are extended back resting alongside the legs. The forehead rests softly onto the earth. The gaze is down and inward.
benefits: Gently stretches the hips, thighs, and ankles. Calms the brain and helps relieve stress and fatigue. Relieves back and neck pain when done with head and torso supported.

name: Corpse
description: The body rests on the earth in a supine position with the arms resting by the side body. The palms are relaxed and open toward the sky. The shoulder blades are pulled back, down and rolled under comfortably, resting evenly on the earth. The legs are extended down and splayed open. The heels are in and the toes flop out. The eyes are closed. Everything is relaxed. The gaze is inward.
benefits: Calms the brain and helps relieve stress and mild depression. Relaxes the body. Reduces headache, fatigue, and insomnia. Helps to lower blood pressure.

name: Crescent Lunge
translation: ashta = side, chandra = moon, āsana = posture
description: From mountain pose, on the inhalation bring the hands up and interlace the fingers together. Exhale, bend to one side, lengthening the opposite of the rib cage and stretch.
benefits: Stretches the rib cage, arms and torso. Tones the oblique muscles.

name: Crow
description: From an inverted position, with the hips up and the head down, the arms are bent in a 90-degree angle with the knees resting on the elbows. The palms are firmly rooted into the earth with knuckles pressed firmly into the earth for support. The belly is pulled up and in towards the spine with the ribcage and chin lifted. The weight of the body shifts slightly forward as the toes lift up and off the earth into the full expression of the pose. The gaze is down and slightly forward.
benefits: Strengthens arms and wrists. Stretches the upper back. Strengthens the abdominal muscles. Opens the groin. Tones the abdominal organs.

name: Dolphin
translation: pīñcha = feather, mayūra = peacock, āsana = posture
description: From Downward-Facing Dog, the forearms are planted onto the earth with the elbows narrow and the palms down in a Sphinx position. The pelvis is tucked. The ribcage lifted. The feet are rooted and the legs are straight with the tailbone in dog tilt. The gaze is down and slightly forward.
benefits: Calms the brain and helps relieve stress and mild depression. Energizes the body. Stretches the shoulders, hamstrings, calves, arches, and hands. Strengthens the arms and legs. Helps relieve the symptoms of menopause. Relieves menstrual discomfort when done with the head supported. Helps prevent osteoporosis. Improves digestion. Relieves headache, insomnia, back pain, and fatigue. Therapeutic for high blood pressure, asthma, flat feet, sciatica, and sinusitis. Warms up the ankles and the toes.

name: Downward-Facing Dog
translation: parivṛtta = revolved, adho = downward, mukha = facing, śvāna = dog, āsana = posture
description: From downward_dog.html the legs are straight with the sits bones tilted up and reaching for the sky. The feet are flat with the heels firmly rooted. One palm is flat with the knuckles evenly pressed into the earth. The other hand reaches under the body and grasps the opposite ankle. The spine is long and the heart is open toward the sky. The neck is loose and the crown of the head is relaxed toward the earth. The gaze is toward the center.
benefits: Calms the brain and helps relieve stress and mild depression. Energizes the body. Stretches the shoulders, neck, hamstrings, calves, arches, and hands. Strengthens the arms and legs. Helps relieve the symptoms of menopause. Relieves menstrual discomfort when done with the head supported. Helps prevent osteoporosis. Improves digestion. Relieves headache, insomnia, back pain, and fatigue. Therapeutic for high blood pressure, asthma, flat feet, sciatica, and sinusitis.

name: Eagle
description: From a standing position the one thigh is crossed over the other with the toes and/or the ankle hooked behind the lower calf. The weight of the body is balanced on the standing foot. The arms are crossed in front of the torso so that one arm is crossed above the other arm. The top arm is tucked into the elbow crook of the bottom arm. The hands are hooked around each other as well. Once hooked, the elbows lift up and the fingers stretch towards the ceiling. The gaze is soft and forward.
benefits: Strengthens and stretches the ankles and calves. Stretches the thighs, hips, shoulders, and upper back. Improves concentration. Improves sense of balance.

name: Extended Hand to Toe
translation: utthita = extended, hasta = hand, pādāṅguṣṭha = big toe, āsana = posture
description: From mountain.html pose, lift one foot. Bend forward and catch the toes with the fingers. Place the other hand on the hip to square the hip towards the front. Slowly straighten the knee and the torso and open the leg to one side. Use a strap if necessary. Gaze towards the front or opposite of the extended leg for balance.
benefits: Opens the hips and groins. Stretches the hamstrings, IT bands and legs. Improves balance.

name: Extended Side Angle
translation: utthita = extended, pārśva = side, koṇa = angle, āsana = posture
description: From warrior II the lower body stays static while the upper body is folded forward at the crease of the hip. One arm is extended toward the front with the bicep by the ear and the fingers spread wide while the other reaches down to the earth on the inside of the thigh. The upper torso and the gaze twist up towards the sky.
benefits: Strengthens and stretches the legs, knees, and ankles. Stretches the groin, spine, waist, chest, lungs, and shoulders. Stimulates abdominal organs. Increases stamina.

name: Forearm Stand
translation: pīñcha = feather, mayūra = peacock, āsana = posture
description: From an inverted position, with the body perpendicular to the earth, the weight of the body is supported on the forearms that are parallel and pressed firmly into the earth. The palms are flat. The knuckles are evenly pressed into the earth. The fingers are spread wide. Both legs reach up toward the sky in a straight line with the pelvis tucked. The ribcage is lifted. The gaze is forward.
benefits: Strengthens arms and shoulders. Improves focus and balance. Stretches the upper and lower back. Strengthens the abdominal muscles. Tones the abdominal area.

name: Forward Bend with Shoulder Opener
description: From a standing position, the body is folded over at the crease of the hip with the spine long. The neck is relaxed and the crown of the head is towards the earth. The feet are rooted into the earth. The toes are actively lifted. The spine is straight. The ribcage is lifted. The chest and the thighs are connected. The sacrum lifts up toward the sky in dog tilt. The fingers are interlaced behind the body and the palms are together. The arms and elbows are straight. The shoulder blades rotate towards each other as the hands move forward (away from the lower back). The gaze is down and inward.
benefits: Calms the brain and helps relieve stress and mild depression. Stimulates the liver and kidneys. Stretches the hamstrings, calves, and hips. Strengthens the thighs and knees. Improves digestion. Helps relieve the symptoms of menopause. Reduces fatigue and anxiety. Relieves headache and insomnia. Relieves headache and insomnia. Opens the shoulders.

name: Half-Moon
description: From a standing position one leg is straight while the other is extended back parallel to the earth (or a little above parallel) and one hand is on the earth (beyond the little-toe side of the foot, about 12 inches) while the other hand is extended up towards the sky. The shoulder blades are squeezed together and the fingers move outward in opposing directions. The weight of the body is supported mostly by the standing leg while the bottom hand has very little weight on it but is used intelligently to regulate balance. The upper torso is rotated open to the sky. Both hips are externally rotated. Energy is extended actively through the flexed toes to keep the raised leg strong. The inner ankle of the standing foot is lifted strongly upward, as if drawing energy from the earth. The sacrum and scapulae are firmly pressed against the back torso and lengthen the coccyx toward the raised foot. The gaze is either up or down, depending on the condition of the neck. If injured the gaze is down.
benefits: Strengthens the abdomen, ankles, thighs, buttocks and spine. Stretches the groins, hamstrings, calves, shoulders, chest and spine. Improves coordination and sense of balance. Helps relieve stress. Improves digestion.

name: Handstand
translation: adho = downward, mukha = facing, vṛkṣa = tree, āsana = posture
description: In this inverted posture the weight of the body is on the hands - shoulder-width apart with fingers forward and parallel to each other (if the shoulders are tight, the index fingers are turned out slightly). The shoulder blades are firm against the back torso and pulled up toward the tailbone. The upper arms are rotated outward with the eye of the elbow to the front of the room to keep the shoulder blades broad while the outer arms hug inward in opposing forces for balance and stability. The palms are spread and the bases of the index fingers are pressed firmly against the earth. Balance is maintained by keeping the Bandhas engaged while pressing the earth away with straight arms and flexed feet. The gaze is down and forward.
benefits: Strengthens the shoulders, arms and wrists. Stretches the belly. Improves sense of balance. Calms the brain and helps relieve stress and mild depression.

name: Low Lunge
description: The front knee is bent in a 90-degree angle directly above the ankle and the back knee is resting on the earth with the top of the back foot pressed firmly into the earth. The hips are squared and pressed forward. The inner thighs scissor towards each other. The pelvis is tucked under to protect the low back. The ribcage is lifted. The arms are lifted. The hands can be together or separated and facing each other with the fingers spread wide. The gaze is forward.
benefits: Stretches the chest, lungs, neck, belly and groin (psoas). Strengthens the shoulders, arms and back muscles. Strengthens and stretches the thighs, calves and ankles.

name: Pigeon
translation: supta = supine, kapota = pigeon, āsana = posture
description: Lie on the back in supine position. Bend the knees, heels close to SI bones and cross one ankle over the opposite knee. Thread the hands or reach through between the thighs. Lift the foot off the floor and hold the bent knee behind the thigh or shin to bring it closer to the chest, make sure that the acrum is rooted to the floor.
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and quads. If the elbow is used to push the thigh, it opens the hips as well.

name: King Pigeon
translation: eka = one, pāda = foot or leg, rāja = king, kapota = pigeon, āsana = posture
description: From a seated position with the hips squared, one leg is extended forward with the knee bent and parallel to the earth. The front heel is rooted close to the groin (or extended out in a 90 degree angle if flexibility allows). The other leg is extended back with the knee bent and perpendicular to the earth. The back foot is hooked on the inside of the elbow of the back arm. The front elbow is bent upward perpendicular to the earth with the bicep by the ear. The fingers are interlaced to connect the bind behind the body and assist in opening the chest. The gaze is natural and forward.
benefits: Stretches the thighs, groins (psoas), abdomen, chest, shoulders and neck. Stimulates the abdominal organs. Opens the shoulders and chest.

name: Plank
description: The body is parallel to the earth. The weight of the body is supported by straight arms and active toes. The abdomen is pulled up towards the spine and the pelvis is tucked in. The neck is a natural extension of the spine and the chin is slightly tucked. The palms are flat and the elbows are close to the side body. The joints are stacked with the wrists, elbows and shoulders in a straight line perpendicular to the earth. The gaze follows the spine and the eyes are focused down.
benefits: Strengthens the arms, wrists, and spine. Tones the abdomen.

name: Plow
description: From a supine position, the upper back rests on the earth with the hips and legs revolved back over the torso above and beyond the head towards the earth. The torso is perpendicular to the earth. The legs are fully extended with no bend at the knees as the toes reach for the earth. The hands are either supporting the lower back or extended behind the back on the earth with extended elbows and fingers interlaced (as flexibility allows), opening the shoulders. The neck is straight. The chin tucked. Do not look to the side as this may injure the neck. The is gaze inward.
benefits: Calms the brain. Stimulates the abdominal organs and the thyroid glands. Stretches the shoulders and spine. Helps relieve the symptoms of menopause. Reduces stress and fatigue. Therapeutic for backache, headache, infertility, insomnia, and sinusitis.

name: Pyramid
translation: pārśva = side, uttāna = stretch out, āsana = posture
description: From a standing position with one leg forward and one back lean the torso forward at the crease of the hip joint. Stop when the torso is parallel to the floor. Press the fingertips or flat palms to the floor on either side of the front foot, maintaining a straight elongated spine. If it isn’t possible to touch the floor, or to maintain a straight spine, support the hands on a pair of blocks. Press the thighs back and lengthen the torso forward, lifting up through the top of the sternum. Then, as flexibility allows, bring the front torso closer to the top of the thigh without rounding the spine. Eventually the long front torso will rest down on the thigh. The gaze is down.
benefits: Calms the brain. Stretches the spine, the shoulders, the hips and the hamstrings. Strengthens the legs. Stimulates the abdominal organs. Improves posture and sense of balance. Improves digestion.

name: Reverse Warrior
translation: pārśva = side, vīrabhadra = warrior, āsana = posture
description: From warrior II , the lower body stays static while the upper body arches back in a gentle back bend. The top arm is extended back with the bicep by the ear and the fingers spread wide. The other arm slides down the back leg resting on the thigh or shin, but not the knee joint. The gaze is up towards the sky.
benefits: Strengthens and stretches the legs, knees, and ankles. Stretches the groin, spine, waist, chest, lungs, and shoulders. Stimulates abdominal organs. Increases stamina. Relieves backaches, especially through second trimester of pregnancy. Therapeutic for carpal tunnel syndrome, flat feet, infertility, osteoporosis, and sciatica.

name: Seated Forward Bend
translation: paśchima = back, uttāna = stretch out, āsana = posture
description: From a seated position with the sits bones rooted into the earth the legs extend forward to the degree that the chest and thighs can stay connected. The fingers wrap around the toes. The upper torso folds forward at the crease of the hips with the spine long. The gaze is forward.
benefits: Calms the brain and helps relieve stress and mild depression. Stretches the spine, shoulders and hamstrings. Stimulates the liver, kidneys, ovaries and uterus. Improves digestion. Helps relieve the symptoms of menopause and menstrual discomfort. Soothes headache and anxiety. Reduces fatigue. Therapeutic for high blood pressure, infertility, insomnia and sinusitis. Traditional texts say that Paschimottanasana increases appetite, reduces obesity and cures diseases.

name: Lotus
description: Bring the bottom ankle and place it on top of the opposite knee, both ankles will be resting on top of the thighs.
benefits: Opens the hips, groin and stretches the knees, ankles and thighs. Strengthens the back and calms the mind, reduces stress and anxiety. Improves circulation and blood flow in the pelvis.

name: Half Lord of the Fishes
translation: ardha = half, matsya = fish, indra = king
description: Begin in a seated position. Bend one knee so the sole of your foot is close to the opposite inner thigh. Bend your opposite knee in, foot on the floor, heel to the outside of your bent thigh. Extend your arm (same side of your Lotus leg) high into the sky and begin to twist it to the outside of your bent knee. Use your opposite hand as leverage to twist deeper. Hook your elbow to the outside of your thigh and gaze over your back shoulder. If you want to extend your twist deeper, wrap your arm around the shin of your bent knee and sweep your opposite arm around to meet it. Catch opposite fingertips or the wrist. Keep a long spine.
benefits: Stretches the shoulders, the chest, the thighs, the groins, and the abdomen. Strengthens the legs and the ankles. Improves balance.

name: Shoulder Stand
translation: sa = with, ālamba = support, sarvāṅga = all limb, āsana = posture
description: From a supine position, the upper back is resting on the earth with the hips straight up towards the sky. The torso is perpendicular to the earth. The legs are fully extended and the toes are active. The hands are either supporting the lower back or extended up by the side body in matchstick. The neck is flat on the earth and the chin is tucked in. The gaze is inward.
benefits: Calms the brain and helps relieve stress and mild depression. Stimulates the thyroid and prostate glands and abdominal organs. Stretches the shoulders and neck. Tones the legs and buttocks. Improves digestion. Helps relieve the symptoms of menopause. Reduces fatigue and alleviates insomnia. Therapeutic for asthma, infertility, and sinusitis.

name: Side Plank
translation: vasiṣṭha = name of a sage, āsana = posture
description: From an arm balance position the weight of the body is supported on one side and distributed equally between the bottom arm and foot while the other (top) arm lifts with fingers spread wide and the other (top) foot stacks on top. The grounded (bottom) foot is flat and gripping the earth from the outside edge of the foot. If flexibility of the foot is limited then instead of gripping the earth with a flat foot, the weight of the body is balanced on the side edge of the foot that is flexed instead of flat. The arm supporting the weight of the body and the grounded foot actively press into the floor as the shoulder blades firm against the back and then widen away from the spine drawing toward the tailbone. Bandhas are engaged to maintain balance and stability. The crown of the head reaches away from the neck and the gaze is up towards the hand.
benefits: Calms the brain and helps relieve stress and mild depression. Stretches the shoulders, hamstrings, calves, and arches. Strengthens the arms and legs. Helps relieve the symptoms of menopause. Helps prevent osteoporosis. Improves digestion. Relieves headache, insomnia, back pain, and fatigue. Therapeutic for high blood pressure, asthma, flat feet, sciatica.

name: Sphinx
translation: sālamba = supported, bhujaṅga = serpent, āsana = posture
description: From a prone position with the pelvic bowl is firmly contracted interiorly towards the center line of the body while the pubis is tucked under. The legs are extended back and the tops of the feet are flat. The palms are flat and the elbows are on the mat, stacked right below the shoulders. On an inhalation, lift the sternum and extend the neck away from shoulders with the elbows, palms and pelvic bone firmly attached to the mat.
benefits: Strengthens the spine. Stretches the chest, the lungs, the shoulders and the abdomen. Stimulates the abdominal organs. Opens the heart and the lungs.

name: Splits
description: The hips are parallel and squared to the earth with one leg extended forward. The opposite leg extended back with the knee and foot squared to the earth. The inner thighs scissor towards each other. The hands are by the side body or at the heart center in Anjali Mudra (Salutation Seal) or stretched straight up toward the sky. The ribcage is lifted. The heart is open. The gaze is forward.
benefits: Stretches the thighs, hamstrings, and groin. Stimulates the abdominal organs.

name: Garland Pose
translation: mālā = garland or necklace, āsana = posture
description: From a squatting position the feet are as close together as possible (keep your heels on the floor if you can; otherwise, support them on a folded mat). The thighs are slightly wider than the torso. The torso is leaning gently forward and tucked snugly between the thighs. The elbows are pressed against the inner knees and the palms are together in Anjali Mudra (Salutation Seal). The knees resist the elbows to help lengthen the front torso. The gaze is soft and forward.
benefits: Stretches the ankles, groins and back torso. Tones the belly.

name: Standing Forward Bend
description: From a standing position, the body is folded over at the crease of the hip with the spine long. The neck is relaxed and the crown of the head is towards the earth. The feet are rooted into the earth with the toes actively lifted. The spine is straight. The ribcage is lifted. The chest and the thighs are connected. The sacrum lifts up toward the sky in dog tilt. The fingertips are resting on the earth next to the toes. The gaze is down or slightly forward.
benefits: Calms the brain and helps relieve stress and mild depression. Stimulates the liver and kidneys. Stretches the hamstrings, calves, and hips. Strengthens the thighs and knees. Improves digestion. Helps relieve the symptoms of menopause. Reduces fatigue and anxiety. Relieves headache and insomnia.

name: Crescent Moon
translation: ashta = side, chandra = moon, āsana = posture
description: From mountain pose, on the inhalation bring the hands up and interlace the fingers together. Exhale, bend to one side, lengthening the opposite of the rib cage and stretch.
benefits: Stretches the rib cage, arms and torso. Tones the oblique muscles.

name: Side Splits
translation: upaviṣṭha = seated, koṇa = angle, āsana = posture
description: From a wide stance the legs are open and extended sideways to your degree of flexibility. The outer edges of the feet are rotated and gripping toward the earth. The weight of the body is supported by the arms. The palms are rooted into the earth with the fingers pointing towards the body. There should be no excess weight on the knee or ankle joints as you lower down to your degree of flexibility. The gaze is down and slightly forward.
benefits: Stretches the insides and backs of the legs. Stimulates the abdominal organs. Strengthens the spine. Calms the brain. Releases groin.

name: Tree
description: From a standing position, one foot is rooted into the earth with the opposite heel rooted into the inner thigh with the toes pointing towards the earth. The pelvis and the chin are tucked in. The arms are lifted above the head with the palms together in prayer position. The gaze is forward.
benefits: Strengthens the legs, ankles, and feet. Improves flexibility in the hips and knees. Improves balance.

name: Triangle
description: From a standing position, the legs are straight and separated into a wide stance. The feet are aligned and flat on the earth with the back foot in a 60-degree angle towards the front. The inner thighs are rotated externally away from each other. The pelvis is tucked and the ribcage is lifted. One arm extends up towards the sky as the other reaches down to the earth. Both arms are aligned with the shoulders in a straight line. The fingers reach out as the shoulder blades squeeze together. The gaze is toward the front.
benefits: Stretches and strengthens the thighs, knees, and ankles. Stretches the hips, groin, hamstrings, calves, shoulders, chest, and spine. Stimulates the abdominal organs. Helps relieve stress. Improves digestion. Helps relieve the symptoms of menopause. Relieves backache, especially through second trimester of pregnancy. Therapeutic for anxiety, flat feet, infertility, neck pain, osteoporosis, and sciatica.

name: Upward-Facing Dog
translation: ūrdhva = upward, mukha = facing, śvāna = dog, āsana = posture
description: The body is in a prone position parallel to the earth. The weight of the body is supported equally by the straight arms and the tops of the feet which press firmly into the earth. The shoulders are rotated back and down. The ribcage is lifted and pulled thru to the front in a slight upper thoracic backbend. The joints are stacked with the wrists, elbows and shoulders in a straight-line. The neck is a natural extension of the spine and the chin is slightly tucked. The abdomen is pulled up towards the spine. The palms are flat and the elbows are close to the side body. The gaze is forward.
benefits: Improves posture. Strengthens the spine, arms, and wrists. Stretches the chest, lungs, shoulders, and abdomen. Firms the buttocks. Stimulates abdominal organs. Helps relieve mild depression, fatigue, and sciatica. Therapeutic for asthma.

name: Warrior One
description: From a standing position, the legs are in a wide stance with the feet aligned and flat on the earth. The back foot is in a 60-degree angle towards the front. The hips are squared. The inner thighs are rotated towards each other. The front knee is bent in a 90-degree angle directly above the ankle. The arms extend up to the sky with the biceps by the ears. The hands can be together or separated and facing each other with the fingers spread wide. The ribcage is lifted and the pelvis tucked. The gaze is forward.
benefits: Stretches the chest, lungs, shoulders, neck, belly and groin (psoas). Strengthens the shoulders, arms and back muscles. Strengthens and stretches the thighs, calves and ankles.

name: Warrior Two
description: From a standing position, the legs are separated into a wide stance. The front knee is bent in a 90-degree angle directly above the ankle. The back leg is extended and straight with the outside edge of the back foot gripping the earth in a 60-degree angle towards the front. The inner thighs are externally rotated away from each other. The pelvis is tucked. The ribcage is lifted. The arms are extended out to the sides and are aligned with the shoulders in a straight line with the fingers reaching out as the shoulder blades squeeze together. The gaze is toward the front fingers.
benefits: Strengthens and stretches the legs and ankles. Stretches the groin, chest, lungs, and shoulders. Stimulates abdominal organs. Increases stamina. Relieves backaches, especially through second trimester of pregnancy. Therapeutic for carpal tunnel syndrome, flat feet, infertility, osteoporosis, and sciatica.

name: Warrior Three
description: From a standing position, one leg is rooted and perpendicular to the earth while the other leg is raised, extended back and parallel to the earth. The head of the thighbone of the standing leg presses back towards the heel and is actively rooted into the earth. The arms and the extended leg lengthen in opposing directions with Bandhas engaged. The hips are squared and the tailbone presses firmly into the pelvis. The arms, torso, and extended raised leg should be positioned relatively parallel to the floor. The gaze is forward or down.
benefits: Strengthens the ankles and legs. Strengthens the shoulders and muscles of the back. Tones the abdomen. Improves balance and posture.

name: Wheel
translation: ūrdhva = upward, dhanu = bow, āsana = posture
description: Pressed up from a supine position, lying on your back, the palms are rooted into the earth with the fingers pointed towards the heels. The feet are grounded. The hips are pressed up. The thighs are rotated inward. The thoracic spine is arched creating a strong crescent arch along the spinal column. The gaze is forward.
benefits: Strengthens the arms, wrists, legs, buttocks, abs, and spine. Stimulates the thyroid and pituitary. Increases energy and counteracts depression. Therapeutic for asthma, back pain, infertility, and osteoporosis.

name: Wild Thing
translation: camatkāra = struck with wonder, āsana = posture
description: From downward dog pose, elevate one leg toward the sky and stack the corresponding hip over the other hip. Bring the upper heel as close to the buttocks as possible. The hips remain stacked; then bring the shoulders forward slowly over the hands. Replace the corresponding hand to the upraised leg with the other hand and flip yourself over and extend the top hand forward. The bottom foot is now facing toward the front of the mat and you remain on the ball of the top foot and the corresponding knee is bent. Continue to lift hips up towards the sky and continue reaching the free hand towards the front of the room and slightly downwards. Allow the head to curl back.
benefits: Stretches the chest, shoulders, back, and throat. Strengthens and opens the hips, hip flexors, and thighs.

name: Big Toe Pose
description: From a standing forward fold, hook the first two fingers around each big toe. Lengthen the spine on an inhale, then fold on the exhale, drawing the crown towards the floor.
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and calves and calms the mind.

name: Gorilla Pose
description: In a forward fold, slide the palms face up under the soles of the feet so the toes reach the wrists. Bend the elbows to ease the torso closer to the legs.
benefits: Deepens the hamstring stretch and releases the wrists.

name: Bird of Paradise Pose
description: From a bound side angle with the arms clasped around a bent leg, walk the feet together and root through the standing leg. Slowly straighten the bound leg out to the side while lifting the chest tall.
benefits: Builds standing balance and opens the hips, hamstrings and shoulders.

name: Revolved Bird of Paradise Pose
description: From a revolved bound side angle, stand tall onto the standing leg and extend the bound leg forward and out while the torso stays twisted away.
benefits: Joins a deep twist with standing balance and a strong hamstring opening.

name: Upward Salute
description: From mountain, sweep the arms overhead with the palms facing or touching. Lift through the fingertips while grounding evenly through the feet.
benefits: Lengthens the spine and opens the shoulders and chest.

name: Standing Foot Behind the Head Pose
description: Standing on one leg, hook the other leg behind the neck and shoulders, then rise to stand tall with the hands at the heart.
benefits: Demands deep hip opening and single leg balance.

name: Standing Foot to Head Pose
translation: of the three steps of Vishnu
description: Balancing on one leg, hold the raised foot and draw it up alongside the head. Keep the standing leg strong and the chest lifted.
benefits: Opens the hamstrings intensely and builds standing balance.

name: Standing Foot Behind the Head Forward Bend Pose
description: With one leg hooked behind the head, fold forward over the standing leg and reach the hands towards the floor.
benefits: Combines extreme hip opening with a deep forward fold.

name: Half Standing Forward Bend Pose
description: From a forward fold, inhale and lift the torso halfway, fingertips to the shins or floor. Lengthen the spine flat and draw the shoulders back.
benefits: Lengthens the spine and strengthens the back.

name: Standing Half Bound Lotus Forward Bend Pose
description: Place one foot high on the opposite thigh in half lotus and bind the same hand behind the back to that foot. Fold forward over the standing leg.
benefits: Opens the hips and shoulders and challenges balance in a fold.

name: Goddess Pose
description: Step the feet wide and turn the toes out. Bend the knees out over the ankles into a deep squat while the arms lift with the elbows bent.
benefits: Strengthens the legs and opens the hips and groin.

name: Revolved Half Moon Pose
description: Balancing on one leg with the other lifted behind, place the opposite hand to the floor and twist the torso open, the top arm reaching up.
benefits: Improves balance and wrings out the spine.

name: Extended Standing Hand to Big Toe Pose
description: Standing on one leg, hold the big toe of the raised leg and open that leg out to the side. Keep the chest lifted and the hips level.
benefits: Builds balance and opens the hips and hamstrings.

name: Revolved Standing Hand to Big Toe Pose
description: Holding the raised foot with the opposite hand, extend the leg forward and twist the torso away from it.
benefits: Joins balance with a standing twist and hamstring stretch.

name: Standing Hand to Big Toe Pose
description: Standing tall on one leg, hold the big toe of the lifted leg and straighten it out in front. Keep both hips level and the spine long.
benefits: Strengthens the standing leg and stretches the hamstrings.

name: Mountain Pose
description: Stand with the feet together or hip width and ground evenly through all four corners of the feet. Stack the spine tall and let the arms rest by the sides.
benefits: Improves posture and body awareness and anchors all standing poses.

name: Standing Splits Pose
description: From a forward fold over one leg, lift the other leg high behind you with the hands framing or holding the standing ankle.
benefits: Opens the hamstrings and builds standing balance.

name: Dancer  Pose
description: Standing on one leg, hold the inside or outside of the back foot and kick it up and back as the chest lifts and the free arm reaches forward.
benefits: Opens the chest, shoulders and thighs and builds balance.

name: Revolved Triangle Pose
description: In a short stance, square the hips over the front leg and twist, bringing the opposite hand to the floor and the top arm to the sky.
benefits: Strengthens the legs and improves spinal mobility.

name: Wide Legged Forward Bend I Pose
description: With the feet wide and parallel, hinge from the hips and fold, bringing the hands to the floor between the feet and the crown towards the ground.
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and inner legs.

name: Wide Legged Forward Bend II Pose
description: From the wide stance, place the hands on the hips and fold forward with a long spine, keeping the chest open.
benefits: Stretches the legs while strengthening the back.

name: Wide Legged Forward Bend III Pose
description: In the wide stance, interlace the hands behind the back and fold forward, letting the clasped arms fall over the head.
benefits: Opens the shoulders and stretches the hamstrings.

name: Wide Legged Forward Bend IV Pose
description: From the wide stance, fold and hold the big toes with the first two fingers, bending the elbows to draw the crown down.
benefits: Deepens the hamstring and inner leg stretch.

name: Revolved Wide Legged Forward Bend
description: Folded in a wide stance, walk both hands to one foot and twist the torso open, the top arm reaching to the sky.
benefits: Adds a twist to the forward fold and frees the spine.

name: Side Wide Legged Forward Bend
description: In a wide fold, turn towards one leg and fold over it, drawing the torso along the thigh.
benefits: Stretches one hamstring deeply at a time.

name: Archer's Pose
description: Seated with the legs extended, hold both feet, then draw one foot up towards the ear like pulling a bowstring while the other leg stays long.
benefits: Opens the hips and hamstrings and builds seated balance.

name: Bound Angle Pose
description: Seated, bring the soles of the feet together and let the knees fall out to the sides. Hold the feet and lengthen the spine tall.
benefits: Opens the hips and inner thighs.

name: Both Feet Behind the Head I Pose
description: Seated, work one leg at a time behind the head and hook the ankles together behind the neck, then balance with the hands at the heart.
benefits: Demands extreme hip opening and a strong, rounded spine.

name: Cow Face Pose
description: Seated, stack one knee over the other and draw the heels beside the hips. Reach one arm up and one behind the back and clasp the hands between the shoulder blades.
benefits: Opens the shoulders, chest and outer hips.

name: Easy Pose
description: Sit cross legged with the shins loosely crossed and the feet under the knees. Rest the hands on the thighs and lengthen the spine.
benefits: Calms the mind and opens the hips for seated breathing and meditation.

name: Fire Log Pose
description: Seated, stack the shins one directly over the other so the ankles rest on the knees, then fold forward to deepen the stretch.
benefits: Opens the outer hips deeply.

name: Embryo in Womb Pose
description: From lotus, thread the arms through the gap behind the knees and hold the face, then balance on the tailbone and rock gently.
benefits: Opens the hips intensely and builds core control.

name: Foot Behind the Head I Pose
description: Seated, lift one leg and hook it behind the head and shoulders, then sit tall with the hands at the heart.
benefits: Opens the hips and hamstrings intensely and strengthens the spine.

name: Foot Behind the Head II Pose
description: With one leg hooked behind the head, fold forward over the extended leg and reach for the foot.
benefits: Adds a deep forward fold to an intense hip opener.

name: Seated Forward Bend I Pose
description: Seated with the legs extended, hinge from the hips and fold forward, holding the feet or shins with a long spine.
benefits: Stretches the whole back body and calms the mind.

name: Seated Forward Bend II Pose
description: In the seated forward fold, hold the sides of the feet and draw the chest towards the thighs.
benefits: Deepens the hamstring and back stretch.

name: Seated Forward Bend III Pose
description: In the seated forward fold, wrap the first two fingers around the big toes and lengthen forward.
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and spine.

name: Seated Forward Bend IV Pose
description: In the seated forward fold, clasp one wrist beyond the feet and settle the torso onto the legs.
benefits: Encourages a deep, quiet forward fold.

name: Seated Half Bound Lotus Forward Bend Pose
description: Place one foot in half lotus on the opposite thigh and bind that hand behind the back to the foot, then fold over the extended leg.
benefits: Opens the hips and shoulders within a forward fold.

name: Seated Three Limbed Forward Bend Pose
description: Seated, fold one shin back beside the hip like hero pose and extend the other leg, then fold over the straight leg.
benefits: Stretches the hamstring and the front of the folded thigh.

name: Seated Gate Pose
description: Kneel on one knee and extend the other leg out to the side. Reach the top arm over the ear and side bend towards the straight leg.
benefits: Stretches the side body and the inner legs.

name: Head to Knee I Pose
description: Seated, fold one shin in with the sole to the inner thigh and extend the other leg. Fold forward over the straight leg with a long spine.
benefits: Stretches one hamstring at a time and calms the mind.

name: Head to Knee II Pose
description: In head to knee pose, tuck the bent foot under the seat and fold forward over the extended leg.
benefits: Opens the ankle and hamstring.

name: Head to Knee III Pose
description: In head to knee pose, turn the bent foot so the sole faces up under the thigh, then fold forward.
benefits: Opens the hip and hamstring deeply.

name: Hero Pose
description: Kneel with the knees together and the feet just outside the hips, then sit the seat down between the heels and lengthen the spine.
benefits: Stretches the thighs and ankles and improves posture.

name: Heron Pose
description: Seated, fold one shin back beside the hip and hold the other foot, then draw that straight leg up towards the face.
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings intensely.

name: Noose Pose
description: In a deep squat, twist the torso and wrap both arms around the knees, binding the hands behind the back.
benefits: Twists the spine and opens the shoulders and ankles.

name: Half Pigeon Pose
description: From all fours, slide one shin forward under the torso and extend the other leg back, sitting the hips towards the floor.
benefits: Opens the outer hip and hip flexors.

name: Sage Marichi's I Pose
description: Seated with one knee bent and foot flat, wrap the same arm around the shin and bind behind the back, then fold forward over the straight leg.
benefits: Opens the shoulders and stretches the hamstring.

name: Sage Marichi's II Pose
description: With one foot in half lotus and the other knee bent upright, bind the arm around the bent knee and fold forward.
benefits: Opens the hips and shoulders within a fold.

name: Sage Marichi's III Pose
description: Seated with one knee bent and foot flat, hook the opposite elbow outside the knee and twist, binding the hands behind the back.
benefits: Wrings out the spine and aids digestion.

name: Sage Marichi's IV Pose
description: With one foot in half lotus and the other knee bent, twist towards the bent knee and bind the arms behind the back.
benefits: Deepens the seated twist and hip opening.

name: Side Lunge Pose
description: From a wide squat, shift the weight fully onto one bent leg and extend the other straight to the side, flexing that foot.
benefits: Opens the inner thighs, hips and hamstrings.

name: Front Splits Pose
description: From a low lunge, slide the front heel forward and the back knee back until both legs straighten into a full front splits, hips square.
benefits: Deeply opens the hamstrings and hip flexors.

name: Half Splits Pose
description: From a low lunge, straighten the front leg and hinge forward over it, hips drawing back.
benefits: Stretches the hamstring gently and safely.

name: Wide Splits Pose
description: From a wide stance, lower to the floor and slide the legs apart into a straight line, hips grounded, chest lifted.
benefits: Opens the inner thighs and hips intensely.

name: Staff Pose
description: Seated with the legs extended together, flex the feet, press the hands beside the hips and sit tall through a long spine.
benefits: Builds upright posture and core strength and anchors seated poses.

name: Thunderbolt Pose
description: Kneel with the knees and feet together and sit back onto the heels, spine tall and hands resting on the thighs.
benefits: Aids digestion and steadies the mind.

name: Toe Stand Pose
description: From standing, come onto the ball of one foot, place the other foot in half lotus, and lower into a balanced squat with the hands at the heart.
benefits: Builds ankle strength and balance and opens the hip.

name: Banana Pose
description: Lying on the back, keep the hips grounded and curve the torso and legs to one side into a crescent, holding the top wrist overhead.
benefits: Stretches the whole side body gently.

name: Fish Pose
description: Lying on the back, tuck the hands under the hips, press into the forearms and lift the chest, letting the crown rest lightly on the floor.
benefits: Opens the chest and throat and counters rounded shoulders.

name: Supine Foot to Head Pose
description: Lying on the back, draw one straight leg up and towards the head, holding the foot while the other leg stays grounded.
benefits: Opens the hamstrings deeply with the spine supported.

name: Extended Supine Hand to Big Toe Pose
description: Lying on the back, hold the big toe of the raised leg and open it out to the side towards the floor, keeping the other leg grounded.
benefits: Opens the inner thighs and hamstrings.

name: Supine Hand to Big Toe Pose
description: Lying on the back, hold the big toe of one leg and draw it straight up towards the torso while the other leg stays long on the floor.
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings with a supported spine.

name: Happy Baby Pose
description: Lying on the back, draw the knees towards the armpits and hold the outer feet, stacking the ankles over the knees.
benefits: Opens the hips and releases the lower back.

name: Sleeping Yogi Pose
description: Lying on the back, work both legs behind the head and cross the ankles, then wrap the arms and settle the spine to the floor.
benefits: Opens the hips and spine to their fullest extension.

name: Supine Spinal Twist Pose
description: Lying on the back, draw one knee across the body towards the floor and open the arms wide, gazing away from the knee.
benefits: Releases the lower back and wrings out the spine.

name: Supine Straddle Pose
description: Lying on the back, open both straight legs wide towards the floor and hold the feet or ankles.
benefits: Opens the inner thighs with the spine at rest.

name: Waterfall Pose
description: Lying on the back, lift both straight legs to vertical with the feet flexed, arms resting by the sides.
benefits: Decompresses the legs and calms the body.

name: Wind Removing Pose
description: Lying on the back, hug both knees into the chest and draw the forehead towards the knees if comfortable.
benefits: Releases the lower back and eases the abdomen.

name: Half Bow Pose
description: Lying on the front, hold one ankle and lift that thigh and the chest while the other arm reaches forward.
benefits: Opens the chest and one thigh while building back strength.

name: Cobra Pose
description: Lying on the front with the hands under the shoulders, press lightly and lift the chest, keeping the elbows bent and the lower ribs down.
benefits: Strengthens the spine and opens the chest.

name: Reverse Corpse Pose
description: Lie face down with the arms by the sides and the forehead resting on the floor, letting the whole body soften.
benefits: Calms the body and gently eases the lower back.

name: Puppy Pose
description: From all fours, walk the hands forward and lower the chest towards the floor while the hips stay over the knees.
benefits: Opens the shoulders and lengthens the spine.

name: Frog Pose
description: Lying on the front, bend the knees and hold the tops of the feet, then press them down towards the hips as the chest lifts.
benefits: Opens the thighs, ankles and chest.

name: Locust I Pose
description: Lying on the front with the arms by the sides, lift the chest, arms and legs away from the floor and reach back.
benefits: Strengthens the whole back body.

name: Locust II Pose
description: In locust, reach the arms out to the sides like wings as the chest and legs lift.
benefits: Strengthens the mid back and shoulders.

name: Locust III Pose
description: In locust, extend the arms forward past the head as the chest and legs lift.
benefits: Builds full back body strength and shoulder endurance.

name: Sage Gheranda's Pose
description: From a prone backbend, bend the knees and reach back to hold the feet, drawing them towards the head as the chest lifts.
benefits: Opens the whole front body intensely.

name: Snake Pose
description: Lying on the front, clasp the hands behind the back and lift the chest, drawing the shoulders together.
benefits: Opens the chest and shoulders and strengthens the back.

name: Tortoise Pose
description: Seated with the legs wide and knees bent, slide the arms under the knees out to the sides and fold the torso low towards the floor.
benefits: Opens the hips and hamstrings and quiets the mind.

name: Table Pose
description: From all fours, stack the wrists under the shoulders and the knees under the hips, with a flat, neutral spine.
benefits: Builds a neutral, stable base for many kneeling poses.

name: Eight Point Pose
description: From a low plank, lower the knees, chest and chin to the floor with the hips lifted, eight points touching down.
benefits: Builds upper body strength and prepares for backbends.

name: Humble Flamingo Pose
description: From a standing forward fold on one leg, hook the arms around the standing leg and lift the other leg high behind, bowing the head low.
benefits: Demands deep balance, hamstring opening and humility of effort.

name: Gate Pose
description: Kneel on one knee with the other leg extended to the side, foot on the floor. Reach the top arm overhead and bend towards the straight leg.
benefits: Stretches the side body and inner legs.

name: Horse Pose
description: From a standing half lotus, bend the standing knee deeply and wrap the arms, lowering into a bound, kneeling balance.
benefits: Builds balance and opens the hips and shoulders.

name: Lizard Pose
translation: intense stretch of the front body
description: From a lunge, lower both forearms to the floor inside the front foot and let the hips sink.
benefits: Opens the hips and hip flexors deeply.

name: Lunge Pose
description: Step one foot forward between the hands and lower the back knee or keep it lifted, sinking the front thigh towards parallel.
benefits: Opens the hip flexors and builds leg strength.

name: Crooked Monkey Pose
description: From a low lunge, twist the torso towards the front leg and hook the arm across, reaching towards a bind.
benefits: Adds a deep twist to a lunge.

name: One Legged King Pigeon Pose
description: From a low lunge with the back knee down, bend the back leg and reach both hands overhead to hold the foot, arching the chest open.
benefits: Opens the chest, shoulders, thighs and hip flexors.

name: Upward Plank Pose
description: Seated with the legs extended, place the hands behind the hips and lift the hips towards the sky, pointing the toes to the floor.
benefits: Opens the chest and shoulders and strengthens the back body.

name: Four Limbed Staff Pose
description: From plank, bend the elbows straight back and lower halfway, keeping them hugged to the ribs and the body in one line.
benefits: Builds arm, shoulder and core strength.

name: Flying Warrior Pose
description: From side plank, extend the top leg forward and hold the big toe, straightening the leg out to the side while balancing on one arm.
benefits: Combines arm balance, hamstring opening and standing strength.

name: Extended Side Plank Pose
description: From side plank, lift the top leg and hold the big toe, extending it towards the sky.
benefits: Adds a hamstring stretch to a demanding arm balance.

name: Inverted Staff Pose
description: From a backbend, lower onto the forearms and interlace the hands behind the head, walking the feet out.
benefits: Opens the chest and spine deeply and strengthens the shoulders.

name: Little Thunderbolt Pose
description: Kneeling in a backbend, lower the crown towards the heels while the thighs stay engaged, hands holding the ankles.
benefits: Builds thigh strength and opens the chest.

name: Tiger Pose
description: From all fours, arch the spine and lift one leg back and up, reaching to hold the foot if possible.
benefits: Opens the front thigh and strengthens the back.

name: Both Feet Behind the Head II Pose
description: With both legs behind the head, place the hands to the floor and lift the seat, balancing the weight on the arms.
benefits: Combines extreme hip opening with an arm balance.

name: Chin Stand Pose
description: From forearm balance, arch the spine and lower the chin to the floor as the legs fold overhead towards it.
benefits: A profound backbend and inversion demanding great control.

name: Crane Pose
description: From a squat, plant the hands, lift onto the toes and rest the knees high on the upper arms, then lean forward until the feet float, arms straight.
benefits: Builds arm strength, balance and focus.

name: Deaf Man's Pose
description: From shoulder stand or plow, bend the knees down beside the ears and rest them on the floor.
benefits: Deeply stretches the spine and quiets the mind.

name: Eight Angle Pose
description: Seated, hook one leg over the shoulder, plant both hands, and press up, crossing the ankles and extending them to one side.
benefits: A demanding arm balance blending twist and core strength.

name: Elbow Balance Pose
description: From forearm balance, bend the knees and arch back, lowering the feet towards the head.
benefits: A deep backbend and inversion on the forearms.

name: Elephant Trunk Pose
description: Seated, hook one leg high over the same arm, plant both hands and lift the seat and the other straight leg off the floor.
benefits: Builds arm strength and core control.

name: Firefly Pose
description: From a wide squat, thread the arms behind the knees, plant the hands and press up, extending both legs straight out to the sides.
benefits: Builds arm strength and opens the hamstrings.

name: Floating Stick Pose
description: Seated, plant the hands beside the hips and press the whole body up off the floor with the legs held in staff position.
benefits: Builds intense arm, wrist and core strength.

name: Flying Man Pose
description: From a twist or crow, extend one leg forward past the arm and the other straight back, balancing across both hands.
benefits: A dynamic arm balance combining twist and extension.

name: Revolved Flying Man Pose
description: From a deep twist, hook one thigh over the upper arm and extend both legs, balancing in a twisted arm balance.
benefits: Blends a strong twist with an arm balance.

name: Two Legged Sage Koundinya's Pose
description: From an arm balance, extend both legs out to one side, stacked and straight, balancing across the arms.
benefits: Demands core strength, balance and open hamstrings.

name: Side Crow Pose
description: From a squat, twist the knees to one side and rest them on one upper arm, then lean forward until the feet float.
benefits: Combines a twist with an arm balance.

name: Forearm Balance Pose
description: From forearm balance preparation, place the forearms parallel and kick up to balance the legs straight over the shoulders.
benefits: Builds shoulder strength, balance and confidence upside down.

name: Dragonfly  Pose
description: From a deep twist, hook one leg over the opposite arm and balance the body sideways across both hands with the legs extended.
benefits: A challenging twisted arm balance.

name: Supported Headstand Pose
description: On the forearms with the hands cupping the head, lift the hips and walk the feet in, then float the legs up to vertical.
benefits: Strengthens the core and shoulders and calms the mind.

name: Tripod Headstand Pose
description: With the crown on the floor and the hands planted ahead like a tripod, lift the knees onto the arms and extend the legs up.
benefits: Builds balance and shoulder and core strength.

name: Flying Lizard Pose
description: From a lizard lunge, hook the front shin high on the arm and press into an arm balance, extending the back leg.
benefits: A demanding arm balance built from a deep hip opener.

name: Peacock Pose
description: Kneeling, plant the hands with the fingers facing back, tuck the elbows into the belly and lean forward until the legs and chest float level.
benefits: Builds intense wrist and core strength and aids digestion.

name: Pendant Pose
description: Seated cross legged or in lotus, plant the hands beside the hips and lift the whole body, swinging the legs beneath.
benefits: Builds arm, wrist and core strength.

name: Flying Pigeon Pose
description: From a standing figure four, plant the hands and hook the shin across the arms, tipping forward until the back leg floats.
benefits: A balance blending hip opening and arm strength.

name: Rooster Pose
description: From lotus, thread the arms through the gap at the shins, plant the hands and lift the whole body off the floor.
benefits: Builds arm and core strength from a deep hip opener.

name: Scorpion Pose
description: From forearm balance, bend the knees and arch the spine, lowering the feet towards the head.
benefits: A deep backbend inversion demanding shoulder strength and control.

name: Shoulder Pressing Pose
description: From a squat, thread both arms behind the knees, plant the hands and lift the crossed feet off the floor.
benefits: Builds arm strength and opens the hips.

name: Shoulder Stand with Lotus Legs Pose
description: In shoulder stand, fold the legs into lotus and rest the knees, balancing the folded legs over the hips.
benefits: Combines an inversion with a deep hip opener.

name: Supported Shoulder Stand Pose
description: Lying on the back, lift the legs and hips and support the back with the hands, extending the legs straight up over the shoulders.
benefits: Calms the nervous system and refreshes the legs.

name: Bound Revolved Chair Pose
description: From chair pose, bring the palms together at the heart and hook one elbow across the opposite knee, twisting the chest open.
benefits: Strengthens the legs and wrings out the spine.
